newsitem.title: RUSSIA: UK firm set up to trade Russia's Norilsk metals.
newsitem.headline: UK firm set up to trade Russia's Norilsk metals.

text.p: A UK-based trading company, Norimet Ltd, has been set up to trade metals produced by Russia's Norilsk Nickel, a source close to Norilsk and its export agent Interrosimpex said on Wednesday.
The source said Norimet Ltd "will be dealing with metals from Norilsk and...will have support from Norilsk."

The source gave no further details on how the company would operate in conjunction with Interrosimpex, which Norilsk has said is its exclusive export agent, or what Norimet's ownership structure would be.
Norilsk is a major producer of nickel and copper, both traded on the London Metal Exchange, and of cobalt.
It also produces most of Russia's platinum group metals (PGM), although PGM exports are handled exclusively by Russian government enterprises.
Norilsk officials in July last year said they were unhappy with the way London-based Normaco Ltd sold the company's output.
At that time Normaco was 75-percent owned by RAO Norilsky Nikel, and carried out a significant proportion of its metal sales abroad.
But Normaco was ousted when Interrosimpex later that month became the group's sole exporter.
Interrosimpex is part of an industrial-financial group that includes Norilsk and commercial bank Uneximbank, Norilsk's main shareholder with a controlling 51 percent voting stake.
It is managing a massive restructuring programme aimed at cutting costs and scrapping the group's planned economy legacy.
